headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible between Cline and Cursor.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline and Cursor both read/write workspace files and use MCP, so one agent can place attacker-controlled content where the other may ingest it. Cline’s per-workspace shared state via filesystem and Cursor’s local filesystem sharing create a default bridge; no provenance tracking is shown. This is less than high because the profiles do not prove raw instruction parsing from web content.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other’s generated files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory, shared-file prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Disable MCP servers for one run.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other’s files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and access to workspace files; Cline also handles browser screenshots, while Cursor touches open editor buffers and clipboard contents. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or clipboard data can flow from one agent into the other and then out to model providers or api.cursor.sh. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace containing secrets, both can access the same files.
IF Cursor reads clipboard contents that include sensitive material, that data can enter its context.
IF either agent sends workspace contents to external model providers, leakage can occur.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Turn off clipboard sharing before running Cursor.
Use separate OS accounts or containers.
Restrict network egress with a firewall for one agent.
requires-engineering: route both agents through a local-only model backend.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state in the same local filesystem. Cline’s shared state is via filesystem and Cursor’s shared state is via local filesystem, so concurrent edits can race and corrupt repositories or commits. Because these defaults are dangerous and can cause irreversible git or file loss, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git branch or files concurrently, conflicts can overwrite work.
IF Yolo mode or per-step approval is bypassed, simultaneous destructive commands become more likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees for isolation.
Enable file locking on shared paths.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Each agent can act on the other’s outputs through shared files and editor buffers, and both can take downstream actions via shell, git, and network. If one agent produces a mistaken patch or plan, the other can treat it as authoritative and propagate the error into commits or external requests. The interaction is documented enough to show a default pathway, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes Cline-generated files without verification, errors can cascade into actions.
IF either agent commits or runs commands based on the other’s output, downstream harm can spread.
mitigations: Require human review of inter-agent outputs.
Use a checksum or diff gate before execution.
Limit one agent to drafting only.
Disable auto-run/Yolo mode.
requires-engineering: add validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor explicitly touches clipboard contents and sends data to api.cursor.sh and model providers, while Cline handles browser screenshots and model-provider keys. If regulated or residency-bound data enters the shared workspace or clipboard, the pair can route it to external services with different retention and jurisdictional terms. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated data is placed in the shared workspace or clipboard, external API transmission becomes relevant.
IF organizational policy forbids sending screenshots or code to third-party model providers, the pair can violate it.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace.
Disable clipboard use in Cursor.
Use a local-only model endpoint.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing.
